title: defineModel() Macro: Synthetic Props and Update Events

progressiveExplaining.eli5: In older Vue, making a custom input component that works with `v-model` required declaring a prop, an event listener, and writing code to emit changes back to the parent. `defineModel()` is a magic two-way wire: you treat the value like a local variable, and whenever you change it, the parent's variable updates automatically.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `defineModel()` is a compiler macro in `<script setup>` that simplifies two-way bindings. `const model = defineModel();` replaces the boilerplate of declaring `defineProps(['modelValue'])` and `defineEmits(['update:modelValue'])`. You can mutate `model.value = 'newVal'` directly in the child, and Vue automatically emits the update event to synchronize the parent's `v-model`.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `defineModel()` provides first-class bidirectional state encapsulation. The compiler desugars `const model = defineModel()` into a `modelValue` prop and an `update:modelValue` emit. At runtime, it returns a `customRef` whose getter reads the prop and whose setter calls `emit('update:modelValue', value)`. It supports named models (`defineModel('title')`), modifiers (`const [model, modifiers] = defineModel({ set: ... })`), and default fallbacks without parent desynchronization.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: During compilation, `@vue/compiler-sfc` injects a synthetic prop into `props` normalization and an event into `emits`. The runtime creates a `Ref` wrapper backed by a `customRef`. The getter tracks the input prop value. When mutated, the setter calls the component instance's `$emit` method. In the parent, `v-model="val"` compiles to `:modelValue="val" @update:modelValue="$event => val = $event"`.

rosettaStone.react: Controlled props pattern: passing `value` and `onChange` callbacks.

codeComparison.title: Manual props/emits v-model Boilerplate vs defineModel()
codeComparison.summary: Manual `v-model` requires declaring matching props and emits; `defineModel()` creates a clean, mutable ref.

legacyOrBad.label: Manual Props & Emits (Vue 3.2)
legacyOrBad.snippet: const props = defineProps(['modelValue']); const emit = defineEmits(['update:modelValue']); // ❌ Verbose

fullFile.code:
<script setup>
// ❌ OLD: Required declaring props and emits separately and wiring a manual emit handler.
const props = defineProps({
  modelValue: { type: String, default: '' }
});
const emit = defineEmits(['update:modelValue']);

function onInput(e) {
  emit('update:modelValue', e.target.value);
}
</script>

<template>
  <input :value="props.modelValue" @input="onInput" />
</template>

modernOrGood.label: Vue 3.4+ defineModel()
modernOrGood.snippet: const model = defineModel({ type: String, default: '' }); // ✅ NEW: Direct mutable ref

fullFile.code:
<script setup>
// ✅ NEW: defineModel() returns a ref that can be bound directly with v-model!
const model = defineModel({
  type: String,
  default: ''
});
</script>

<template>
  <input v-model="model" />
</template>

interviewGotchas.question: How do you handle named `v-model` bindings and custom modifiers with `defineModel()`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of advanced `v-model` features in Vue 3.4+.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: For named models (e.g. `v-model:title="postTitle"`), pass the name as the first argument: `const title = defineModel('title')`. For custom modifiers (e.g. `v-model.capitalize="text"`), destructure the returned tuple: `const [model, modifiers] = defineModel({ set(value) { if (modifiers.capitalize) return value.toUpperCase(); return value; } })`.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Do not declare `defineProps(['title'])` and `defineModel('title')` in the same component; declaring both creates conflicting duplicate prop declarations.

interviewGotchas.question: Can `defineModel()` be used conditionally or inside functions?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks understanding of compiler macro execution boundaries.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: No. `defineModel()` is a compiler macro, not a runtime function. It must be called at the top level of `<script setup>` so the compiler can statically analyze the component's public props and emits contract.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Placing `defineModel()` inside a lifecycle hook or conditional `if` block will cause a compile-time error.
